provenance: Original commissioned writing for ClueCrew, authored with the ENG-003 SPaG set. Not adapted from any source.
body:
Maya had never volunteered for anything before, so nobody expected her to run the eco-club.

The idea arrived on a wet Tuesday. She walked past the bins behind the kitchen and noticed that somebody ___(1)___ the paper recycling straight into the general waste. By lunchtime she had spent ___(2)___ hour drawing a plan on the back of her maths book.

“You cannot fix the whole school,” said Dev, “___(3)___ the bins have been like that since Year 3.”

“I am not fixing the whole school,” Maya ___(4)___. “I am fixing one corridor.”

She began with a count. Every lunchtime she stood beside the blue bin and wrote down what people threw away. Crisp packets. A shoe. Two library books, which she returned ___(5)___ the shelf.

On Friday she showed her list to Mr Achebe. He read it twice and stopped smiling.

“Those are library books. ___(6)___ not rubbish,” he said quietly.

“If we painted a picture on every lid,” Maya said, “people ___(7)___ exactly where things go.”

Mr Achebe leaned back in his chair. “They might,” he agreed. “Shall we find out?”

Three weeks later the row of new labels ___(8)___ brighter than anything else in the corridor. Dev had joined the club, although he still refused to give up his apples.
